all_elements_rule.application_here: Element (c) is absent under BOTH the narrow and broad constructions tested (see element chart). Because infringement requires every element to be present, the claim-1-level read-on verdict does NOT depend on how element (d)'s ambiguity ultimately resolves: even under the broadest reasonable construction of element (d), the claim as a whole still does not read on our baseline, because element (c) independently and robustly fails first.

all_elements_rule.statement: To literally infringe, an accused product must contain every limitation of the claim; the absence of a single limitation is dispositive of non-infringement regardless of how the other limitations construe.

This is the one claim-1 element whose read-on verdict is genuinely construction-sensitive: NO under the narrow/plain reading, not-confidently-excluded under the broad, specification-informed reading (~65% VS sits inside two of the three disclosed embodiment ranges for the same 'high volume solids' concept). Claim-language-only observation (Phillips v. AWH, 415 F.3d 1303 (Fed. Cir. 2005) (en banc)): the numeral '70' in claim 1 coincides with the LOW end of the narrowest, most-preferred disclosed sub-range ('70% to about 90%'), which is textually more consistent with claim drafters anchoring 'about 70 percent' to their preferred embodiment than with an intent to sweep the claim down to the outer 50% floor of the broadest generic range -- but this is an inference from drafting convention, not a holding, and the broad reading remains a reasonable alternative a cautious adversary or FTO counsel could press. This element alone is GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS PENDING COUNSEL.

our_baseline_assumed: commodity DGEBA epoxy + dimer-acid reactive polyamide + silica extender + iron-oxide color + naphtha/butanol solvent; two-pack solvent-borne; volume solids ~65% (below 70%); no acrylate-based reactive-compatibilizer component of any kind; cured blooming/blushing rating not measured.
overall_verdict_rationale: Element (c) (reactive compatibilizer agent with polar functionality) is absent from our baseline under BOTH the narrow and broad constructions tested -- silica and iron oxide are inert inorganic fillers/pigments, not reactive organic compatibilizer components, and the specification's own acrylate-based definition of the term narrows rather than widens the broad reading. Under the All-Elements Rule, an accused product must contain every claim limitation to infringe; a single robustly-absent element is dispositive of non-infringement regardless of how any other element (here, element (d), volume solids) construes. The claim therefore does not read on our baseline under either tested construction, and this conclusion is independent of the flagged ambiguity on element (d).

positive_control.evidence: Re-charting element (c) against mutated_baseline_assumed: ours_present flips from False/False (narrow/broad) to True/True, and reads_on_this_element flips from NO/NO to YES/YES under both constructions -- because the planted component is structurally identical to the spec's own named preferred species for the element, it reads on under the narrow (spec-anchored) construction too, not only the broad one. With element (c) now present, the All-Elements Rule no longer has an independently-absent element to rely on, so the claim-level verdict collapses onto element (d) alone: under the narrow construction the claim still does NOT read on (mutated baseline is still ~65% VS, still <70%/<~67-68%), but under the broad construction the claim-level verdict flips from DOES_NOT_READ_ON to GENUINELY_AMBIGUOUS_PENDING_COUNSEL (both elements now construction-sensitive-or-present, and (d) is not confidently excludable). This confirms the adjudication method is NOT vacuously stable -- it correctly propagates a planted element-(c) defect into a changed overall verdict, which is what the method exists to catch.
